items.followUp: State two characteristics of Kingdom Fungi.

rubric.why: Kingdom Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that protists have a true nucleus or are eukaryotic.

rubric.why: Protists are commonly described as mostly unicellular; other textbook characteristics are also acceptable.
rubric.description: Gives one further characteristic of Protista.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are mostly unicellular, aquatic, autotrophic, or heterotrophic.

modelAnswer: Protists are eukaryotic organisms, with a true nucleus.

items.followUp: Give two characteristics of Kingdom Monera.

rubric.why: An autotroph makes its own food, usually using light energy.
rubric.description: Defines autotroph and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an autotroph makes its own food and giving a suitable example, such as a green plant.

rubric.why: A heterotroph obtains food from other organisms.
rubric.description: Defines heterotroph and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a heterotroph obtains food from other organisms and giving a suitable example, such as a human or an animal.

modelAnswer: An autotroph makes its own food; for example, a green plant.
A heterotroph obtains food from other organisms; for example, a human.

items.followUp: Why are chromosomes not distinctly visible during interphase?

rubric.why: During interphase, the genetic material is in a loose chromatin form rather than distinct chromosomes.
rubric.description: Explains why chromosomes are not distinct in interphase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromatin is loose, diffuse, or uncoiled during interphase.

rubric.why: During cell division, chromatin condenses into distinct chromosomes that can be seen.
rubric.description: Explains why chromosomes are visible during cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes during division.

modelAnswer: During interphase, DNA is present as long, thin, uncoiled chromatin, so individual chromosomes cannot be seen distinctly.
During cell division, the chromatin condenses into short, thick chromosomes that become visible.

items.followUp: State two roles of mitosis in living organisms.

rubric.why: Mitosis produces more cells for growth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking mitosis to growth or an increase in cell number.

rubric.why: Mitosis replaces damaged or worn-out cells and also supports asexual reproduction in some organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning repair, replacement of cells, or asexual reproduction.

modelAnswer: Mitosis increases the number of cells and enables growth.
It replaces damaged or worn-out cells and helps in asexual reproduction in some organisms.

items.followUp: What is the role of chlorophyll in a photosystem?

rubric.why: A photosystem is a group of photosynthetic pigments, including chlorophyll, arranged in the thylakoid membrane.
rubric.description: Identifies a photosystem as a pigment-containing unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a group or cluster of pigments in the thylakoid membrane.

rubric.why: The pigments absorb light and pass the energy to the reaction centre.
rubric.description: States the light-absorption or energy-transfer role of a photosystem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it absorbs light energy and transfers it to the reaction centre.

modelAnswer: A photosystem is a group of pigment molecules, including chlorophyll, arranged in the thylakoid membrane.
It absorbs light energy and transfers it to the reaction-centre chlorophyll.

items.followUp: Name the products of alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.

rubric.why: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose, releasing energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing fermentation as the breakdown of glucose without oxygen, with energy release.

rubric.why: The two types are alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.
rubric.description: Names the two types of fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.

modelAnswer: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose to release energy.
Its two types are alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.

items.followUp: What is meant by an enzyme, and how does it affect a chemical reaction?

rubric.description: Identifies an enzyme as a biological catalyst.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an enzyme is a biological catalyst.

rubric.why: Enzymes increase reaction rates by lowering activation energy and are not used up in the process.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of an enzyme on reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes speed up reactions or lower their activation energy.

modelAnswer: An enzyme is a biological catalyst.
It speeds up a biochemical reaction by lowering its activation energy and is not used up in the reaction.

items.followUp: How can a competitive inhibitor affect an enzyme-substrate reaction?

rubric.why: An inhibitor reduces or prevents enzyme activity and therefore slows or stops the reaction.
rubric.description: States the effect of an inhibitor on enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an inhibitor decreases enzyme activity or slows or stops the reaction.

rubric.why: An inhibitor may bind to the enzyme, block its active site, or alter the enzyme's shape so the substrate cannot bind effectively.
rubric.description: Describes how an inhibitor acts on an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it binds to the enzyme, blocks the active site, or changes the enzyme's shape.

modelAnswer: An inhibitor is a substance that decreases or stops the activity of an enzyme.
It may bind to the enzyme and block its active site, or change the enzyme's shape so the substrate cannot bind effectively.
